title: Product ↔ Eng ↔ Applied ML — signal-check & follow-ups (personal prep)
content:
Context and goal:
- Quick personal prep before the cross-functional sync (30m). Primary objective: align on the top-3 delivery risks for H2 model serving roadmap and convert ambiguity into concrete next actions.
- Audience: product PM (Sofia), infra/serving eng lead (Liam), applied ML lead (Diego). Keep it action-focused — avoid rehashing prior decisions.

Meeting logistics (planned)
- Time: 2026-04-16 10:00 PT (30m)
- Format: lightning status (3 slides each / 4 min) + 12 min focused decision/action capture + 5 min wrap
- Pre-reads: short notes below + linked eval summary (ML-2317) + cost projection spreadsheet (confluence:INFR-plt-5021)

Top-level framing (what I want to leave with)
1) A prioritized list of 3 critical unblockers with owners and firm due dates.
2) Agreement on the rollout gating criteria for the new token-caching optimization (who validates outputs / which evals matter).
3) Decision on whether to include quantized 4-bit variant in the first Dedicated rollout or ship as A/B after initial launch.

Proposed agenda (mini)
- 0-3m: quick alignment on meeting outcome and timebox
- 3-12m: Product (Sofia) — customer priorities, contracts that drive SLA/cost targets (what must-not-break)
- 12-21m: Applied ML (Diego) — quality regressions risk from quantization + eval highlights (regression windows, failure modes)
- 21-28m: Serving/Infra (Liam) — latency SLOs, autoscale assumptions, capacity constraints across regions
- 28-30m: capture decisions + owners + due dates

Key notes / talking points to call out
- Product: two enterprise customers (one fintech, one healthcare) asked specifically for <100ms median token latency for short-chat flows and formal audit logs for Private deployments. This anchors our SLA conversation.
- ML: quantization gives ~2.2x throughput/cost improvement on current benchmark but introduces hallucination spike in long-form summarization evals (samples in ML-2317). Need a short prompt-level mitigation or output filter.
- Infra: dedicated pools target TTFB baseline of 80ms median at 8kb context for the standard model; burst capacity assumptions currently require additional reserved GPUs in eu-west-1 for peak traffic.

Open questions I want answers to (quick list)
- Product: which customers are part of the committed launch cohort vs aspirational? Any hard contractual SLOs that constrain rollout date?
- ML: can we produce a 50-sample A/B eval that isolates hallucination triggers by prompt-type by EOW? Who on ML takes this?
- Infra: what's the expected extra monthly cost if we reserve an additional 2x A100-equivalent capacity in eu-west-1 for the first 6 weeks of launch? (rough number please)

Draft decision options (to steer conversation)
1) Conservative path: ship non-quantized model in Dedicated launch, enable quantized variant as canary to 5% traffic for 2 weeks post-launch.
2) Bold path: include quantized 4-bit variant in GA rollout but behind canary traffic-split and strict quality regression alerts that auto-roll back.
3) Split rollout: GA for hosted API only with quantized variant; Dedicated customers get non-quantized for first month.
(Advise: call out customer contracts if they demand non-quantized for auditability.)

Proposed gating criteria for rollout (short list)
- Quality: no >2% absolute drop on intent-classification evals and no >5% relative increase in hallucination rate on long-form summarization for canary traffic window.
- Performance: median token latency delta for quantized variant <= +12ms vs baseline at p50 under steady-state 80rps.
- Ops: successful end-to-end traces for sample requests (trace id log format validated), KMS keyflow tested for Private deployment.

Follow-up action capture (pre-fill — mark owner + due date)
- Diego: run 50-sample A/B hallucination triggers by prompt-type; deliver artifact + example diffs. Due: 2026-04-21.
- Liam: cost delta for reserving 2x extra capacity in eu-west-1 (monthly and 6-week window). Due: 2026-04-18.
- Sofia: flag launch cohort customers and confirm contractual SLOs that might block quantized rollout. Due: 2026-04-17.
- Asha (me): prepare short canary playbook (runbooks + auto-rollback signal thresholds) and one-pager for the exec CT. Due: 2026-04-20.
- Ops/DevRel: surface any customer-managed KMS integration docs with known gaps (tagged). Due: 2026-04-22.

Risks / mitigations I want on the table
- Risk: quantization causes non-deterministic hallucinations in long-form -> Mitigation: run targeted output filters + add explainer attribution probe in canary logs.
- Risk: capacity shortfall in eu-west-1 at peak -> Mitigation: temporary cross-region routing + pre-reserved burst nodes (cost tradeoff).
- Risk: customers object to quantized models for compliance -> Mitigation: provide model checksum + audit log + option to pin non-quantized variant per customer.

Notes-to-self (quick reminders)
- Keep the conversation decision-oriented; if we don't close on owners/dates, escalate to PM sync with exec sponsor.
- Bring a 1-slide backup showing the eval artifacts with concrete examples (will help defuse abstract concerns).
- If Product pushes a hard date, map that to the nearest gating milestone (A/B eval completion, canary stability window).

After-meeting checklist (what I will do within 24-48h)
- Convert captured actions into JIRA tickets (prioritize ML-2317 follow-ups).
- Email a short one-paragraph decisions summary to attendees + exec sponsor, cc infra finance for cost numbers.
- Update the roadmap signal doc with agreed date windows and note "risk: quantization" with owner pointer.

Scribbles / fragment ideas to mention if time allows
- Could we prototype a light-weight per-prompt hallucination detector trained on a curated prompt set? Low effort: heuristic + score threshold for canary.
- Consider a short-term discounting policy for Dedicated early adopters who accept non-quantized baseline during the first 30 days. Helps reduce risk for customers and ops.

End of prep notes. Keep it tight in the meeting — capture live actions in Google doc and paste into JIRA immediately.
